howToRead: A word can match several endings — the LONGEST one wins (it is the most specific). 'Nation' matches -ion and -tion -> use -tion (die, 99.8%); 'Biologie' matches -e and -ie -> use -ie (die, 97%). Each ending's `overriddenBy` lists the more-specific endings that beat it, so overlapping endings (-ion/-tion/-sion, -e/-ie, -eit/-heit/-keit) can be shown together as a family rather than scattered.
scope: The 'Endings' rule type: word-ending rules (some are genuine derivational suffixes with a `why`, others are just spelling patterns — see each ending's `kind`) + the compound rule. This file does NOT contain the app's THEMES (semantic rules: car brands -> der, days/months/seasons -> der, male people & animals -> der, weather -> der). Themes are a separate rule type the app defines on its own and MUST be left untouched — Endings sit alongside Themes and Compounds, not replace them.
source: german-nouns lexicon (~93k nouns, Wiktionary); refined by morphological rules. Compound-head split uses a frequency floor (wordfreq 3.1.1).
sizeWeight: Per-ending display weight in [0,1] for word-cloud-style sizing: 0 = fewest COMMON words covered, 1 = most. Based on `frequentCount` (common single-word nouns whose longest matching ending is this one, Zipf>=3.0). GLOBALLY √-scaled across all genders. INDEPENDENT of tier/accuracy (rule strength) — size = how common the ending is, NOT how reliable. Map to a font size as MIN + weight*(MAX-MIN).

der.note: → der (Baum, Raum, Traum). Virtually no exceptions.
Agent nouns → der (Journalist). The -frist family (die) is split off into its own rule.
der.why: Agent suffix naming a person → der (Journalist).

der.note: French agent nouns → der (Friseur, Ingenieur, Masseur).
der.why: French agent suffix naming a person → der (Friseur).

der.note: Agent nouns → der (Student). The neuter -ment family is split off; das Talent/Patent remain rare exceptions.
→ der (Honig, König). Cardinal numbers (-zig/-ßig) are split off; das Reisig is an exception.
der.why: Productive as an ADJECTIVE suffix; as a noun ending it's lexicalised (der König, Honig).

der.note: Diminutive/agent → der (Frühling, Lehrling). Borrowed English -ing gerunds (Bowling, Styling) are das and remain exceptions.
Agent nouns → der (Demonstrant). das Restaurant / Quant compounds and French loans are exceptions.
→ der (Aktionär, Millionär, Sekretär). das Quartär is an exception.
→ der (Teppich). Exceptions are compounds of das Reich (Königreich, Tierreich).
der.why: A historical suffix, now dead — gender is lexicalised (der Teppich).

der.note: → der (Doktor, Motor, Professor). das Labor / das Tor are exceptions.

Agent nouns → der (Lehrer, Bäcker). Most exceptions follow ANOTHER rule, so reason before memorising: female people → die (Mutter, Tochter, Schwester); non-agent things → das (Wasser, Messer, Fenster, Zimmer). The only ones to simply memorise are feminine for no reason: die Butter, Leiter, Feder, Nummer, Mauer, Steuer.
der.why: Agent/instrument suffix → der (Lehrer, Computer). Root-final -er like Wasser/Mutter is NOT this suffix.

der.note: Leans der (Punkt, Markt, Akt) — but Latin neuters das Produkt/Objekt/Projekt are a big exception group.

die.why: Native suffix forming feminine abstract nouns → die (Möglichkeit).

die.note: Both → die (Nation, Information, Diskussion, Explosion). NB: bare -ion alone is only ~60% reliable — see the separate -ion rule.
→ die (Zeitung, Meinung). A handful of masculine exceptions (der Ursprung, der Schwung).
die.why: Suffix forming feminine deverbal nouns → die (Zeitung, Meinung).
Native suffix forming feminine collective/abstract nouns → die (Freundschaft).

die.note: Abstract nouns → die (Freiheit, Schönheit). Very reliable.
die.why: Native suffix forming feminine abstract nouns → die (Freiheit).

die.note: → die (Natur, Kultur, Literatur, Architektur). Very reliable.
→ die (97%): academic topics (Biologie, Philosophie, Chemie) and most -ie words. Exceptions are loanwords (der Junkie, das Cookie) and das Knie / Genie.

die.why: Bound deverbal form of kommen (ablaut) → die (Zukunft, Ankunft) — not a free suffix.

die.note: Latin abstract suffix → die (Distanz, Toleranz, Tendenz, Konferenz). Native der Tanz/Kranz/Glanz/Lenz are exceptions.

Most nouns ending in -e are die (Schule, Straße, Blume), incl. -ade (Schokolade) and -age (Garage). Exceptions group up: living males → der via the male-people rule (der Junge, Löwe, Affe, Hase); weak-masculine abstracts → der (der Name, Gedanke, Glaube, Wille — and der Name is also a compound head: der Vorname). A few are neuter → das (das Auge, Ende, Interesse) — memorise those, they follow no rule.

Words ending in -in lean die — strongly so for the female suffix -erin/-in (Lehrerin, Freundin, Königin). But many are masculine/neuter: der Termin, das Benzin, das Vitamin, das Cholesterin. And der Schein is a compound head → der Führerschein/Gutschein (the head overrides -in).
die.why: Feminine motional suffix -in/-erin → die (Lehrerin, Königin). The bare -in in der Termin/das Benzin is a different, borrowed ending.

die.note: Activity/place nouns → die (Bäckerei, Polizei, Partei). der Brei / das Allerlei are exceptions.
die.why: Native suffix for activities/places → die (Bäckerei, Polizei).

die.note: → die (Figur, Tour, Spur, Zensur). -tur (Natur/Kultur) and -eur (der Friseur) split off. The common der exceptions are der Flur and der Schwur (and das Dur in music).
ALONE, this is barely a coin flip (~59%): der Champion / Spion / Anion. Trust -tion and -sion, NOT bare -ion. Where it IS der, it's usually a male person (der Champion, Spion).
die.why: Latin action-noun suffix → die — but bare -ion is unreliable (der Spion/Champion are persons).

das.why: Greek -onym ('name') → das (Synonym, Pseudonym) — a real but tiny set.
Romance diminutive -etto/-ette → das (Ballett, Skelett) — borrowed, not productive.

das.note: Latin -mentum → das (Dokument, Element). Distinct from the masculine -ent agent suffix.
Words ending in -um are neuter → das, including -ium (das Studium) and -tum (das Eigentum). A few are masculine: der Reichtum, der Irrtum, der Konsum.
das.why: Latin neuter ending → das (Museum, Studium, Zentrum).

das.note: → das (System, Problem, Morphem). der Atem is irregular; der Moslem is a male person → der.
das.why: Greek -ema ending → das (System, Problem) — a real but unproductive morpheme.

das.note: → das (Modell, Duell, Fell, Kartell). The der exceptions are masculine loanwords: der Appell, der Rebell (a male role), der Quell.
→ das (Material, Potenzial, Editorial, Adverbial). A few obscure der exceptions (Labial).
→ das (Ergebnis, Verständnis, Geheimnis, Zeugnis) — very reliable. A small set are die: die Kenntnis, Erkenntnis, Erlaubnis, Finsternis, Wildnis (memorise these).
Leans das (Paket, Gebet, Gebiet, Filet). Most der exceptions follow a rule: Greek masculines (der Planet, Komet) and male persons (der Prophet, Poet, Athlet). der Magnet/Jet are arbitrary.
Leans das (Brot, Gebot, Angebot, Verbot). The der exceptions are male persons → der (der Pilot, Idiot, Patriot); only die Not is irregular.
Greek -ma leans das (Thema, Drama, Klima, Komma). die Firma is the main exception.
das.why: Greek neuter ending → das (Thema, Drama, Klima).

das.note: Leans das (~56%) — das Auto, Büro, Kino, Video — but this is the WEAKEST ending. Many common words are der (der Euro, Zoo, Cappuccino, Tornado), and the die exceptions include fruits, which follow the fruit rule (die Mango, Avocado). Best learned per word.

compoundRule.note: A compound takes the gender of its LAST noun: das Werk+Zeug, die Auto+Bahn, der Apfel+Kuchen. When in doubt about a long word, look at its final part.
